review_scope: Primary-source check of frozen README/SECURITY dependency origin, licensing, checksum and signature statements; source documents unchanged.

facts: FFmpeg distributes source and links separate Windows binary publishers Gyan and BtbN.
The project describes release source-archive and signed-tag verification.
supported_document_claims: Use the official project download page to find binary publishers.
Distinguish project source signatures from separately built executables.

facts: Base FFmpeg licensing is LGPL 2.1 or later; use of optional GPL components changes the effective license.
The page discusses corresponding source and build configuration for distributed FFmpeg libraries.
supported_document_claims: Review the license and notices for the chosen vendor build; application MIT licensing does not change external dependency terms.

facts: Packages include ffmpeg, ffprobe and ffplay.
Essentials and full builds differ in external library sets; the page identifies the main FFmpeg builds as GPLv3 and supplementary tools as LGPLv3.
The page supplies version and SHA-256 links and currently identifies release 9.0.2.
supported_document_claims: Gyan supplies separate Windows builds with package-specific configuration, license and checksums.
The recorded 9.0.2 essentials provenance is a reviewed test build.

facts: The README describes Windows and Linux builds.
Available variants include GPL, LGPL and nonfree configurations; dependencies and configuration vary.
A floating latest build and daily builds are described.
supported_document_claims: BtbN is a separate binary-build publisher linked by FFmpeg.
Select and review a specific build and its actual license/configuration.

facts: Get-AuthenticodeSignature inspects Authenticode information on Windows.
LiteralPath uses the specified path without wildcard interpretation.
supported_document_claims: Use read-only Authenticode inspection on the exact resolved vendor files and app scripts.

facts: Get-FileHash computes content digests and defaults to SHA256.
supported_document_claims: Compute SHA-256 on exact resolved files and compare with a trusted reference.

explicit_inferences.claim: An FFmpeg source-release signature does not authenticate a separately compiled vendor Windows executable.
explicit_inferences.reason: The project signature applies to the specified source archive/tag, while the Windows executable is a different artifact built and supplied by another publisher.

explicit_inferences.claim: A checksum match identifies reviewed bytes without independently identifying the publisher.
explicit_inferences.reason: Digest comparison establishes content equality against its reference; trusting the origin of the reference is a separate step.

explicit_inferences.claim: Manual trusted setup, same-build executable pairing and checking the actual app-selected path are application guidance.
explicit_inferences.reason: They follow the external dependency execution boundary and inspected Get-ToolPath behavior; they are not represented as vendor certification.

limits: No vendor binaries were downloaded or executed for this source-document check.
No claim that Gyan or BtbN vendor executables have an FFmpeg-project Authenticode signature.
This check supplies primary-source support and does not accept final release assets, physical-device use, or arbitrary future vendor builds.
